\chapter{Comiendo, Viviendo --- Two Families, One Ending}
\label{ch:comiendo}
\hlchaptermodality{237}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can form the gerund of any regular verb.}

I can form the gerund of any regular verb.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[comiendo · viviendo]{comiendo · viviendo — two families, one ending}

\label{lesson:ES-C62-comiendo}



\begin{quote}
\emph{Hablar} gave \emph{hablando}. Now the other two families.
\end{quote}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: -iendo, for both}]
\noindent
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{} & \textbf{} \\
\midrule
\emph{comer} & \emph{\textbf{comiendo}} \\
\emph{beber} & \emph{\textbf{bebiendo}} \\
\emph{vivir} & \emph{\textbf{viviendo}} \\
\emph{escribir} & \emph{\textbf{escribiendo}} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}

One ending for both. Not \emph{-endo} for \emph{-er} and something else for \emph{-ir} — the same \emph{-iendo}, every time.
\end{grammarlens}

\begin{culture}
You have watched this happen before. In the preterite, the \emph{-er} and \emph{-ir} endings turned out to be identical, and the two families you had learned separately quietly became one.

Here it happens again, and more completely: there is not even a difference to notice. So the whole gerund is \textbf{two endings for three verb families}:

\noindent
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{} & \textbf{} \\
\midrule
\emph{-ar} verbs & \emph{\textbf{-ando}} \\
everything else & \emph{\textbf{-iendo}} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}

Two endings, no agreement, no persons. It is the smallest thing this book has asked you to learn, and it unlocks the next chapter entirely.
\end{culture}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hablando}, \emph{comiendo}, \emph{viviendo}
\end{itemize}

\emph{Twice through:}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Which ending do \emph{-er} and \emph{-ir} verbs share? (\emph{\textbf{-iendo}}.)

And how many endings in total? (\textbf{Two}, for three families.)
\end{tcolorbox}
